quickAnswer: San Antonio is an **aerospace NDT town**. Boeing Global Services recruits Level II NDT quality test specialists in San Antonio at a listed **$76K–97K** [1]; StandardAero hires NDT II inspectors and NAS 410 Level 3 engineers [2][3]; and Patriot Aerotech offers an **entry-level NDT apprenticeship** with mentorship toward certification [4]. Formal NDT programs are in Houston and Fort Worth — **San Jacinto College**, **UTI**, **Lone Star College** and **Tarrant County College** [7][9][10][11] — so many locals start with an employer apprenticeship. Texas radiographers are certified under **DSHS rule 25 TAC §289.255** [12].

sections.h2: Why San Antonio is different: aerospace first
paragraphs: Most Texas NDT guides focus on Houston's refineries. San Antonio's NDT market looks very different. Its biggest NDT employers maintain, repair and overhaul aircraft, engines and components — military and commercial — and their technicians work to aerospace standards such as NAS 410 and FAA repair-station requirements rather than refinery codes. That shapes everything from which methods to learn to how hiring works.
It also creates an unusual opportunity: some San Antonio employers hire complete beginners as apprentices and train them to certification, which is less common in other cities.

sections.h2: Who hires NDT technicians in San Antonio
paragraphs: Boeing Global Services has recruited experienced NDT Level II quality test specialists to support its San Antonio business, with a listed salary range of $76,000–97,000 a year [1]. The role involves analysing data, performing routine NDT and documenting results, using eddy current, magnetic particle, penetrant, radiography and ultrasonic methods.

StandardAero, a major aerospace MRO provider, recruits NDT Level II inspectors in San Antonio and promotes on-the-job training and advancement [2]. For senior roles it has sought process engineers who can certify as NAS 410 Level 3 in both penetrant and magnetic particle testing within six months of starting, with five to ten years as a Level 3 in aerospace [3]. Other employers, such as Strategic Technology Institute, have recruited NDI technicians to inspect aerospace weapon-system components and support equipment and to perform fluid analysis [6].
These postings show a clear ladder: apprentice or trainee, Level II inspector in the core aerospace methods, and eventually Level 3 or NDT engineering roles that write procedures and manage programs.

Patriot Aerotech has advertised an NDT Technician Apprentice role in San Antonio supporting aircraft MRO operations, describing it as an entry-level role for people looking to build an NDT career in aerospace [4]. Preferred qualifications include enrolment in or completion of an NDT, aviation maintenance or engineering technology program, the ability to read technical manuals and drawings, willingness to complete required NDT training hours, and the ability to pass background checks, drug screening and customer security requirements; the company offers hands-on training and mentorship toward NDT certification [4].

Patriot Aerotech also operates an FAA Part 145 repair station specializing in NDT services, aviation welding and aerospace fabrication [5]. Working inside a certificated repair station teaches trainees aviation documentation and quality-system discipline early — habits that transfer to any aerospace employer.

Aerospace and defense NDT employers screen candidates carefully. Patriot Aerotech's apprentice posting lists the ability to pass background checks, drug screening and customer security requirements, a valid driver's licence and willingness to work flexible hours including nights or weekends [4]. Work on military aircraft and weapon-system components can involve additional customer security requirements [6].

Preparing for that screening is part of preparing for the job. Keep your record clean, gather documentation of any prior training, and be ready to explain your work history clearly. Candidates who arrive organised and reliable are the ones employers choose to invest in with apprenticeships and paid training.

San Antonio residents who want a college program usually look to Houston or Fort Worth. San Jacinto College offers a pathway of a six-month NDT Technology certificate, a 1.5-year Level 2 certificate and a two-year associate degree [7]. The college quotes PQNDT 2019 survey figures for the South Central region of about $75,000 for Level I, $113,000 for Level II and $131,000 for Level III, while noting that wages depend on experience, method and certifications [8]. San Jacinto also notes that a criminal history could keep graduates from being licensed by the state of Texas [7].

In Houston, Universal Technical Institute runs a nine-month Advanced Non-Destructive Testing Technician program, after which employed graduates typically complete on-the-job training hours with their employers [9], and Lone Star College offers method certificates whose courses exceed SNT-TC-1A requirements [10]. In Fort Worth, Tarrant County College restarted its Nondestructive Inspection, Testing and Evaluation program to serve North Texas industry, which had no other public NDI/NDT program in the area [11].

sections.h2: Which methods matter for San Antonio aerospace
paragraphs: Aerospace MRO relies heavily on fluorescent penetrant and magnetic particle inspection of engine and landing-gear parts, eddy current inspection around fasteners and bolt holes, ultrasonic inspection of components and composites, and radiography for internal features. The Boeing posting lists eddy current, magnetic particle, penetrant, radiography and ultrasonic as top skills [1], and StandardAero's senior roles emphasise PT and MT under NAS 410 [3].
For a beginner, that suggests a clear sequence: PT and MT first, then ET and UT. Etch inspection and FAA-related knowledge are pluses for engine shops [3][6].

Texas regulates industrial radiography through the Department of State Health Services under 25 TAC §289.255, which sets radiation safety requirements and licensing and registration procedures for industrial radiography [12]. DSHS lists the certifications it accepts for industrial radiographers [13] and administers its own industrial radiography certification exams [14].

Aerospace radiography in San Antonio is often performed in shielded facilities, while oil and gas pipeline radiography in South Texas is field work; both require the radiographer to meet DSHS certification requirements, and trainees typically start as radiographer trainees under supervision.

sections.h2: How NDT certification actually works for San Antonio trainees
paragraphs: The most common misunderstanding about NDT training is that a school certifies you. In the United States, the documents most employers follow are ASNT's Recommended Practice SNT-TC-1A, the ANSI/ASNT CP-189 standard and the CP-105 topical outlines [22]. Under SNT-TC-1A, certification is employer-based: a school or online course supplies the classroom hours, but your employer's written practice, its Level III and your documented on-the-job experience are what turn training into a certification. Training programs therefore combine formal classroom or online theory with on-the-job training (OJT) performed in a field or lab setting [22].

In practice, a new technician in any city follows the same ladder: complete Level I and then Level II classroom hours for a method, log supervised experience, pass the employer's general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and receive Level II certification in that method. Level III — the person who writes procedures, approves techniques and certifies others — requires additional experience and, for most employers, the ASNT NDT Level III examinations.

sections.h2: Training hours you will need by method
paragraphs: SNT-TC-1A publishes recommended minimum classroom hours by method and level for high-school-educated candidates [15]. Employers can adopt stricter numbers in their written practice, and aerospace employers working to NAS 410 or customers with their own specifications often do. Visual testing shows the scale of supervised experience involved: SNT-TC-1A recommends 8 training hours for VT Level I and 16 more for Level II, with 70 and 140 hours of experience in the method respectively [16].

sections.h2: Industrial radiography: the extra licensing layer in San Antonio
paragraphs: Radiography is the one method where federal and state radiation-safety law sits on top of SNT-TC-1A. Under 10 CFR 34.43, a licensee may not let anyone act as a radiographer until the person has received training in the required radiation-safety subjects, completed at least two months of on-the-job training and been certified through a radiographer certification program by a certifying entity [17][18]. ASNT's Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel (IRRSP) program is one such certifying entity; it combines a computer-based exam with an employer-conducted practical exam and vision check, and many states recognize it [19]. Online radiation-safety courses such as AWS's roughly 40-hour eLearning module can supply the classroom portion, but site-specific training from the employer is still required [20].

In Texas, DSHS implements these requirements through 25 TAC §289.255 and its own certification exams [12][14]. Confirm with your employer whether it expects the state exam or an accepted third-party certification.

Published industry guidance puts classroom training for a single method at roughly USD 600–2,000, with examination fees of roughly USD 200–500 on top [21]. ASNT lists the initial IRRSP combination exam for radioactive-material and X-ray radiography at USD 260 for members and USD 285 for non-members [19]. Longer certificate and associate-degree programs cost more but bundle several methods, labs and job placement support, and community-college options are often eligible for financial aid.

Before paying, ask whether the price includes the practical hours, specimens and exam fees, whether the course is written to SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 or NAS 410, and whether the provider will document your hours in a form an employer's Level III can accept.

sections.h2: How to choose an NDT training provider
paragraphs: Use this checklist to compare schools, online courses and employer programs.
bullets: Training hours that meet or exceed the SNT-TC-1A table for each method and level.
Hands-on labs with real-flaw specimens, not just slides and videos.
Instructors who hold ASNT Level III in the method they teach.
Documentation of hours suitable for an employer's written practice.
A path to OJT — employer partnerships, apprenticeships or placement support.
For radiography, preparation for IRRSP or the state radiographer exam.
Transparent total cost including exams, books and specimens.

paragraphs: NDT's workforce is ageing: the PQNDT salary and benefits survey put the average NDT technician's age at 47 [23]. As experienced technicians retire, employers across energy, aerospace, infrastructure and manufacturing need trained replacements, which is why so many now sponsor training, apprenticeships and on-the-job programs for motivated newcomers.
One route that fits the local market:
bullets: Apply for an aerospace NDT apprenticeship or trainee role [4].
Complete PT and MT classroom hours, ideally NAS 410-aligned.
Add eddy current and ultrasonic training as your employer allows.
Aim for Level II in the core aerospace methods to compete for roles like Boeing's [1].
Consider a Texas college program for broader credentials [7][9].
Keep a personal logbook of every inspection, method and hour so your experience transfers if you change employers.
Ask employers whether they sponsor Level II exams and NAS 410 certification, and how long that typically takes.

faqs.q: Is there NDT training in San Antonio?
faqs.a: Many San Antonio employers train on the job — for example through aerospace NDT apprenticeships [4]. College programs are in Houston and Fort Worth [7][9][11].

faqs.q: Who hires NDT technicians in San Antonio?
faqs.a: Aerospace MRO employers such as Boeing Global Services, StandardAero and Patriot Aerotech [1][2][4].

faqs.q: How much do NDT Level II technicians earn in San Antonio?
faqs.a: One Boeing Level II posting listed $76,000–97,000 a year [1]; pay varies with methods, certifications and shift.
The aerospace standard for NDT personnel qualification; StandardAero requires NAS 410 Level 3 certification for some senior roles [3].
The Texas Department of State Health Services under 25 TAC §289.255 [12][13].

faqs.q: How long is San Jacinto College's NDT program?
faqs.a: Six months for the certificate, 1.5 years for the Level 2 certificate and two years for the AAS [7].
